How it’s calculated: on a flotation size the first number is the overall diameter in inches and the second is the section width. Sidewall = (overall diameter − rim diameter) ÷ 2. Circumference = π × overall diameter; revolutions per mile = 1,609,344 ÷ circumference (mm), per km = 1,000,000 ÷ circumference (mm). Calculated from the size, not manufacturer-tested values.

Size guide

How it works

01

Find your size

Use the finder at the top of this page, or read the size right off your sidewall. 402 metric size combinations are in the catalog, plus light-truck and flotation sizes.

02

Check price & stock

In the full catalog, 2,777 of the 4,027 listings carry a price today, and every listing shows its full spec sheet — load index, speed rating, weight, tread depth, max pressure. Listings without a price say so instead of guessing.

03

Get them mounted

Pick your set and we’ll mount and balance them. Rotations and flat repairs keep them wearing evenly long after the sale.

Reading your sidewall

Every tire carries its size in the same format. Take the most common size in the catalog:

215/60R16
215 — WidthThe tread’s width in millimeters, sidewall to sidewall.
60 — Aspect ratioSidewall height as a percentage of the width. Higher rides softer; lower handles sharper.
16 — Rim diameterThe wheel size in inches the tire is built to fit.

How the calculations work

The diameter, sidewall, circumference, and revolution figures in each card’s Specifications are size-based calculations, not manufacturer-tested rolling values. Size alone does not establish load capacity, speed capability, inflation pressure, approved rim width, tread depth or tire weight. Check the vehicle placard and manufacturer specifications before changing sizes.

Metric size: sidewall (mm) = section width × aspect ratio ÷ 100. Overall diameter (mm) = rim diameter × 25.4 + 2 × sidewall. Circumference = π × overall diameter. Revolutions per mile = 1,609,344 ÷ circumference (mm); revolutions per km = 1,000,000 ÷ circumference (mm).

Flotation size: the first number is nominal overall diameter in inches and the second is nominal section width in inches. Sidewall = (overall diameter − rim diameter) ÷ 2. Equivalent aspect ratio = sidewall ÷ section width × 100; this is derived, not a sidewall marking or a guaranteed metric-size equivalent.

Conversion: 1 inch = 25.4 mm. Display values are rounded; calculations use unrounded numbers.

Services

Mounted, balanced, looked after

Buying the tire is half the job. The other half is fitting it right and keeping it that way.

  • MountingNew tires fitted to your wheels with fresh valve stems, torqued to spec.
  • BalancingComputer balancing on every install, so there’s no shake at highway speed.
  • RotationRegular rotations even out wear between front and rear — especially on front-wheel-drive cars and loaded trucks.
  • Flat repairPunctures in the tread area patched and plugged properly, and checked before we call it done.
